LOL I sometimes wonder what life would have been like had I not entered the private sector. I'd actually entered the private sector before doing my defense and I never had time to march for my diploma. (I've a PhD.)

Prior to about my 6th year, I was absolutely convinced I was going to be a math teacher, preferably at a small, private, New England college where I'd drive a cranky antique Saab on the weekends while my Volvo wagon would be my daily driver. I had it all picked out, this life I was going to lead.

Fortunately (maybe?), by then, I was starting to get strange people coming to me and offering to help fund my research. I went from being told I was an idiot to being offered money - some even offering me money to remain in academia and do my post doc work there.

It was pretty early on when I made a discovery - something nobody told me, but I figured out from a comment. My math teacher saw me working on finding the area of right triangles and he said to me, "You know you can just square those, find the area, and divide that in half." It was then that I realized that mathematics was a language - the philosophy would come later, and that arithmetic was just one way of saying something with the language.

I wasn't suddenly a math genius. In fact, math still pretty much sucked and, back then, I was going to be a Rock N Roll star. Oh, I was, too... I was also convinced of that. My life is right full of misconceptions, but I digress...

Instead, it was then that I realized it's a language and that it was telling me a story. It was telling me how to reason something, or at least how to find the answer to a puzzle.

Since then, I've looked at many things and have "reduced" them to math. I still made some illogical choices, and some of those worked out surprisingly well, but I've come to appreciate how math can be used to describe so many things. It can tell both truths and lies, stories and facts, news and even weather. It tells sports news, political news, and describes the wonder that is the universe.

I am grateful that I love mathematics, because I can't imagine what my life would have been like had it not been for that teacher. I try, but I keep reverting to the silly notion that I'd have been a rock star and would be old, washed up, and throwing out bad political one-liners. I'm actually more grateful for the math.
